newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arab ministers start talks on Israel, maybe Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Arab ministers start talks on Israel, maybe Iraq.

text.p: Arab foreign ministers met on Friday at the start of two days of talks on the stalemate in Middle East peace talks and probably the U.S.-Iraq confrontation.
Egypt and the Palestinians called the meetings weeks ago, before Baghdad's military involvement in northern Iraq -- closed to its forces for five years -- triggered the current Gulf crisis.
Arab League Secretary General Esmat Abdel-Meguid said on Thursday the crisis was not on the agenda for the formal Arab League meeting on Saturday but any country can raise any subject.
Iraqi Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf arrived on Friday but did not take part in the evening meeting, which was confined to Arab states that attended an Arab summit in June.
Egypt did not invite Iraq to that summit because some Gulf states would not sit beside representatives of the government which invaded Kuwait in 1990.

Egypt wanted the Friday meeting to review new Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's behaviour since the summit warned that Arabs could reconsider their steps in the peace process if Israel does not fulfil its part of the bargain.

Egypt wants Arab opinions on whether there is any point in hosting the Middle East economic summit in November given the lack of progress on the peace process. President Hosni Mubarak said on Thursday he wanted the summit, provided it would be a success.
A significant absentee this time is Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Saud al-Faisal, who sent a junior representative.
If ministers discuss the U.S. attacks on Iraq, Sahaf will find the vast majority sympathetic to Baghdad's view that it has every right to defend its sovereignty and territorial integrity.
Alone of Arab states, Kuwait has supported the United States as it brings new forces into the Gulf, possibly for further attacks on Iraq.

But Sahaf, speaking at Cairo airport on Friday, hinted that Baghdad would not seek to mobilise Arab support: "The protection of Iraq is the responsibility of its people and not the responsibility of any other country."
On Saturday, when Iraq joins and meetings take place under Arab League auspices, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will brief the ministers on his troubles with Israel.
Diplomats said he would complain of Israel's restrictions on the movement of Palestinians and its failure to honour promises made by the previous government of Shimon Peres.

They said Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara might report on an Israeli-U.S. proposal or new talks between Israel and Syria. Shara said on Thursday Syria would reject talks unless Israel honoured previous understandings.
